title: One chromosome before and after replication
alt: Replication doubles DNA amount without initially doubling chromosome number. The two sister chromatids remain one replicated chromosome until they separate. Lettered identification version; answer key is not drawn.
reviewNote: Follow each letter or its leader line. Use the model assumptions and units shown.

title: Mitosis in a model cell: 2n = 4
alt: Four replicated chromosomes align individually; sister chromatids separate. Each daughter nucleus receives four chromosomes. Blue and orange identify parental origins, not different cell types. Lettered identification version; answer key is not drawn.
reviewNote: Follow each letter or its leader line. Use the model assumptions and units shown.

title: Meiosis: separate homologues, then sisters
alt: A diploid 2n = 4 model begins after replication. Meiosis I produces two haploid cells with replicated chromosomes. Meiosis II separates sisters into four haploid products. Lettered identification version; answer key is not drawn.
reviewNote: Follow each letter or its leader line. Use the model assumptions and units shown.

title: Crossing over involves non-sister chromatids
alt: Two replicated homologues contain four chromatids. Exchange between one chromatid from each homologue can produce two recombinant and two unchanged chromatids. Lettered identification version; answer key is not drawn.
reviewNote: Follow each letter or its leader line. Use the model assumptions and units shown.

title: Nondisjunction: compare the gamete outcomes
alt: For one affected chromosome, a meiosis I error produces two n + 1 and two n − 1 gametes; a one-cell meiosis II error produces two normal, one n + 1 and one n − 1 gamete. Lettered identification version; answer key is not drawn.

title: Alternation of generations
alt: Spores grow into gametophytes by mitosis. Fertilization restores diploidy, and mitosis grows the zygote into a sporophyte. Lettered identification version; answer key is not drawn.
